newsitem.title: USA: Maine Public Service cuts dividend.
newsitem.headline: Maine Public Service cuts dividend.

text.p: Maine Public Service Co on Friday said the outage of the Maine Yankee nuclear power plant forced it to cut its quarterly dividend by 45 percent to $0.25 per share.
The utility said it also decided to reduce its 1997 construction budget by about 20 percent to $2.8 million from a previously authorized $3.5 million.

The company said it reduced the dividend because of a drop in its earnings and cash flows because of the outage. The plant was shut down on December 6 to correct electrical cable problems. Operations at the 910-megawatt power plant are expected to resume this summer after the replacement of fuel assemblies.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent owned by New England Electric System, 20 percent owned by Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro-Electric Co, five percent by Maine Public Service Co and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
